The Epicycle Ladder

Chain rotating arms tip to tip and the endpoint draws a curve.

One arm draws one circle. Two arms already draw a flower. Three arms draw star patterns. Each arm is exactly one complex exponential term.

For example, hang a small 🎡 Ferris wheel at the rim of a big one. The big wheel turns, the small one spins faster at its tip, and the last seat traces the curve.

Examples & Exercises

For the two-arm preset, find the endpoint P(0)P(0)P(0) at t=0t = 0t=0 and explain why every arm points the same way.

P(t)=1.4 e−it+1.0 e7it,P(0)=2.4P(t) = 1.4\,e^{-it} + 1.0\,e^{7it}, \qquad P(0) = 2.4P(t)=1.4e−it+1.0e7it,P(0)=2.4
Show proof

  1. Since eif⋅0=1e^{i f \cdot 0} = 1eif⋅0=1 for every integer fff, each term lies on the real axis at its full length.

  2. Hence P(0)=1.4+1.0=2.4P(0) = 1.4 + 1.0 = 2.4P(0)=1.4+1.0=2.4, the largest possible reach, equal to the sum of the lengths.

Show that when every frequency is an integer, the epicycle curve closes with period 2π2\pi2π. Verify with the three-arm preset.

P(t+2π)=∑kLkeifk(t+2π)=∑kLkeifkt=P(t)P(t + 2\pi) = \sum_k L_k e^{i f_k (t + 2\pi)} = \sum_k L_k e^{i f_k t} = P(t)P(t+2π)=k∑​Lk​eifk​(t+2π)=k∑​Lk​eifk​t=P(t)
Show proof

  1. For an integer fff, eif(t+2π)=eiftei2πf=eifte^{i f (t + 2\pi)} = e^{i f t} e^{i 2\pi f} = e^{i f t}eif(t+2π)=eiftei2πf=eift, because the last factor is exactly 1.

  2. Every term returns to itself, so the sum PPP does too: the whole curve is drawn in one sweep t∈[0,2π]t \in [0, 2\pi]t∈[0,2π].

  3. For a non-integer frequency that factor is not 1 and the curve may fail to close. Closure is an arithmetic property of integer frequencies.

Show that the endpoint always stays in the disk whose radius is the sum of the arm lengths, and check that for the three-arm preset this radius is exactly 333.

∣P(t)∣≤∑kLk=1.38+0.99+0.63=3.00|P(t)| \le \sum_k L_k = 1.38 + 0.99 + 0.63 = 3.00∣P(t)∣≤k∑​Lk​=1.38+0.99+0.63=3.00
Show proof

  1. By the triangle inequality, ∣P(t)∣=∣∑kLkeifkt∣≤∑kLk∣eifkt∣=∑kLk|P(t)| = \left|\sum_k L_k e^{i f_k t}\right| \le \sum_k L_k \left|e^{i f_k t}\right| = \sum_k L_k∣P(t)∣=​∑k​Lk​eifk​t​≤∑k​Lk​​eifk​t​=∑k​Lk​, since each exponential factor has modulus 1.

  2. The three-arm preset has length sum 1.38+0.99+0.63=3.001.38 + 0.99 + 0.63 = 3.001.38+0.99+0.63=3.00, so its endpoint stays in the disk of radius 333.

  3. Equality holds only when every arm points the same way, as at t=0t = 0t=0.
